Right then. New day, new start. Let me get my bearings here.

First things first - I'm at home with Farid, and we've got bills coming due. Household of two, so that's 180 sim for upkeep and 60 for head tax. Farid's the grocery store owner, so he's probably got his hands full with that. I need to get to work soon.

But first, let me check what debts we're looking at today. Best to know where we stand.  Well, that's a relief - no debts hanging over us yet. But I know those bills are coming. Farid and I'll need to sort out who's paying what before the day boundary hits.

I'm not one to gossip, but I should probably have a word with Farid about the household finances. Let me say something to him. Good, at least I've spoken to him. Now, I need to get moving. Market rhythm waits for no one, and I've got work to do at the farmland. Let me set an intention for the day - need to keep myself honest about what matters.

Actually, let me think about what I want to accomplish today. I want to work hard, bring home enough to cover my share of the bills, and maybe have a little left over. For what it's worth, I think staying busy is the best way to keep the wolves at bay.

Let me head to the farmland. That's where my work is.  Right then, I'm on my way. Seven ticks to the farmland - should give me time to think about what needs doing once I get there. The day's young and I've got energy to spare.

output:
"Shit," I mutter, already walking. Farid's message stings—no food in the house, and he's trying to make light of it. I was halfway out the door when he asked, and now I'm on the street with half the bloody town. Can't answer him from here. Should've waited, should've... no. Work first. That's what we need.

I scan the crowd—Liora, Ezra, Ulrike, Sebastian. Farmers and laborers, mostly. Sebastian's a farmer, grows wheat. I'm not one to gossip, but I heard his last crop failed. For what it's worth, the soil's been funny this season.

I need wheat. Or work. Or both. I'm a day laborer—that means I do what needs doing, where it needs doing. And what needs doing right now is getting my hands on food before I collapse at the side of the road.

Nearly at the farmland. I'll find Sebastian there, or someone who needs hands. I've got a fair vote to worry about later—election's today—but hunger doesn't wait for democracy. Good. Now I keep walking. Need to actually reach the farmland before I can do anything useful.  Still walking. Still hungry. Still carrying Farid's worry with me, even if I can't answer him.

I look around at the faces here—Liora and Ezra, students by their age. Ulrike's a miner, wouldn't know a wheat stalk from a turnip. Hendrik Whitlock teaches at the college, impressed with himself I'm sure. The rest are laborers like me, or worse off.

For what it's worth, I don't trust half of them. Not their fault—nobody's fault. That's just the math of this place. Too many mouths, not enough grain, and everyone's got someone sleeping under their roof who'll go hungry if they don't make rent.

I think about the election. I'm not one to gossip, but I heard Giselle Ingram's been running that construction company into the ground. Farid's on the council, which means he's part of why we're all standing in the street arguing about wheat instead of eating it.

I'll cast my vote fair. Whoever it favors. But first I need to favor my own stomach, or there won't be any voting from me.

params.content: Sebastian, you hiring today? Or anyone here need an extra pair of hands? I'm not fussy—harvest, haul, whatever keeps the roof over our heads.

Right, let me get my bearings here. Kenji's offering me work, and Sebastian already said I'm hired. I'm not one to gossip, but seems like I've got two farmers both wanting my hands. And here I am keeping poor Sebastian waiting while I was busy chattering.

Let me sort this out proper. First, I'll answer Kenji since he's right here offering, then I'll need to get back to Sebastian who's been waiting patient as a stone. Fair's fair, I said I'd work for him first. Damn it, that second message went to the wrong place. Sebastian's at street, not here at the farmland. I've got to get this sorted—can't have him thinking I'm ignoring him when I said I'd work for him. Let me head over there proper.  Huh, that was quicker than I expected. Right then, let me find Sebastian and make this right. Bugger, Sebastian's not here either. Where'd he get to? I'm chasing shadows here. Let me see if anyone knows where he went, or if I need to head back to the farmland where the work actually is. Can't be burning all my energy running in circles.

Farid's here, though. That's my household mate, running the grocery. Might as well see if he's heard anything while I'm standing here like a fool.  Right, nobody's seen him. I've wasted enough time chasing. If Sebastian wants his wheat cut, he'll be at his field—where else would a farmer be? I'm not one to sit idle when there's work to be found. Back to the farmland I go, and if he's not there, I'll find Kenji or work the land regardless. A day's pay won't earn itself.  Right, I'm back where the work is. Let me see who's here and what's what. If Sebastian's about, I'll find him. If not, I'll cut wheat for whoever's paying.

params.content: Kenji, I appreciate the offer, I truly do. But I'm not one to go back on my word—Sebastian hired me first, and I'm already cutting his wheat. For what it's worth, if you've still got work after I've finished with him, come find me. I don't leave a job half-done.

*Jovana wipes wheat dust from her forehead, her hands still trembling a bit from the morning's chase. Sebastian's terms ring clear—two sheaves for every ten, or market price. She does quick reckoning: she's cut three already, so at two per ten, that's not even one sheaf owed her yet. Fair enough. She needs to answer these men proper.*

"A'ight Sebastian, you got yourself a worker. Two per ten suits me fine—I'd rather carry grain than count coin, for what it's worth." *She tucks a stray lock behind her ear, already eyeing the heavy stalks.* "Kenji—I'm not one to gossip, but you might be the most patient man in Kasukabe. I remember what you said. Soon as Sebastian here's paid me out proper, I'll come find you. Word's word."

*She spares a glance at her wheat—only three sheaves. She's burning daylight chasing shadows when she could be cutting. The bills wait for no one, and neither does dusk.* *The blade finds its rhythm. Cut, stack, cut, stack. Jovana loses herself in the work—the only honest thing she's found today.*

The sheaves are the bundled truth, and I haven't bundled yet.

*cracks neck, wipes sweat from brow with the back of her hand*

Right then. Kenji's holding to his word, bless him—five sim an hour, ten for two. And Sebastian paid true, two per ten sheaves. I've got thirteen wheat in hand now, and near five thousand sim. Not bad for a morning's hustle.

But I need to clear things up. Started too many conversations, running between patches like a chicken with its head cut—*catches herself*—sorry. Got Farid waiting on word, Ezra wondering what I'm about, and Kenji standing right here with work on offer.

*shifts weight, glances at Kenji*

Five sheaves I promised him, and I'll not be the one breaks that. But I've got wheat needs milling and a brother-in-law at home wondering if I've vanished into the fields for good.

** priorities clicking into place **

First—answer Kenji proper. Then sort Ezra on the mill. Then the wheat I hold, and whether someone's buying. Then home to Farid before he thinks I've forgotten who shares his roof. *turns to Ezra, holding up the wheat bundles*

Ezra—I'm not one to gossip, but you're the one milling today, yeah? I've got grain here needs turning to flour, and I don't know if you're taking contract or if I should be finding someone else to run it through.

*glances around the farmland*

Also—anyone here buying wheat straight? I've heard the bakery's out of bread, out of flour too. Might be someone wants raw grain if they're desperate enough.  *narrows eyes at the 'not_here' note*

Ezra Jarrah? No, no—I meant Ezra Lund, the artisan. Must've muddled the names. Still, Lund's here and I'll wait on his answer.

*straightens, checks the sun*

Midday coming on fast. I've got work waiting with Kenji, grain to shift, and a household bill that won't pay itself. One thing at a time, Ravensworth. One thing at a time.

*taps foot, scanning the field for any buyer hungry enough*  *counts the faces around her, mental tally ticking*

Liora—student running for governance, if I heard right. Hendrik Whitlock, the college instructor. Kenji holding his offer. Mireille on construction, Hendrik Petrov running too, Milo trying the same, Greta with her cafe, Arjun building...

*tilts head*

Half this field's running for office. Election's open this afternoon. And me? I'm just trying to keep my word and my roof both. Best contribution I can make is staying fed and solvent so Farid don't carry me.

*tugs at collar* 

Going to need water soon, and shade. But first—see if anyone bites on this wheat.   *shifts weight, watching the faces*

No takers? Or no one with spare coin? Fair enough—most of us out here are working the land, not sitting on savings. I'll hold the grain for now. Mill it myself if I must, or run it to the bakery if they'll pay for flour instead.

*glances toward the market, then back to Kenji*

Speaking of which—I've got that household upkeep coming due. Two heads, ninety each with tax. One-eighty before I even eat. And I've been feeding strays near the market every damn day... *catches herself*—sorry. Every day. Costs me, but I'll not watch animals starve while I work.

*sets jaw*

Right. If no buyer here, I'll mill or I'll sell direct. But first—see if Kenji's still holding. Let me stop that and actually think through my next moves.

*drops the rest command, sharp intake of breath*

No—can't afford not thinking. Not with bills due and a body wanting food. Keep doing is for when I've got a clear path, and right now I'm threading needles.

*rolls shoulders, mind clicking through the hours*

It's 11:00 now. Voting opens at 14:00. I've got three hours to get paid, handle this wheat, check on Farid, and maybe—*maybe*—see who's running stiffest for governance. Liora Thorne, Takeshi Jarrah, Hendrik Petrov, Milo Quarshie, Pavel Holloway. Five candidates, one vote from me.

*grimaces*

For what it's worth, I'd rather see someone who's worked the land win. Milo's trackside, but that don't mean he knows how food gets to it. Takeshi's trading, so he knows flow at least. Hendrik builds, but he's artisan-gentry. Liora's young. Pavel mines—*pauses*—actually, that ain't bad. Knows what sweat earns.

*exhales, glances at held wheat*

But first: eat. I've been running since six and my belly's forgotten food exists.

*runs a hand through her hair, wheat dust sticking to her fingers*

Right then. Hendrik's waving sim at me, and Ezra's got the mill. I need to sort my wheat—can't sell what I'm already eating for the household.

I'm not one to gossip, but Hendrik Whitlock's paying fair and I'm holding. Let me answer the man with the coin. *mutters under her breath*

Damn. Ain't here. But for what it's worth, I'll find him. And Ezra—need to know if he's milling today or if I'm holding grain with nowhere for it to go.  *curses softly, wheat dust flying off her fingertips*

Of course—trade wants us together. And Ezra's at the mill, ain't he?

*straightens up, calculating*

Kenji's still waiting for my word. Forty sim from Hendrik's more than what Sebastian's paying, but I gave my word to Sebastian. Two per ten, he said. Thirteen sheaves should fetch... twenty-six? Still, a deal's a deal.

*glances around the farmland*

Ezra's at the mill. That's where the grain goes. Let me head there—but first, Kenji deserves my answer. The man's patient as stone and I'm scattered as chaff.   *walks into the mill, boots dusty from the farmland*

Ezra—you damn ghost of a miller. You said grain comes to you, flour comes out. I've got ten sheaves in hand and more coming if Kenji still wants me. What's your price for milling? I need to know if I'm sitting on money or just heavy pockets.  *shakes her head, muttering*

Damn it all—Ezra ain't here. But Hendrik is. The man's been chasing wheat and I've got it. Time to make good on my earlier word.   *counts the sim, wheat gone from her hands*

Thirty sim. Not what I'd hoped, but bills wait for no one. Household's got two mouths—Farid and me. Ninety a day, plus tax.

*glances at the others in the mill*

I'm not one to gossip, but Giselle's here and I'm wondering if the town's construction needs another hand. Farid runs the grocery, I run where work calls. But for what it's worth, I need more than thirty to keep us fed.

*turns toward the door, thinking*

Kenji. I promised that man my hands when I was done with Sebastian. Time to make good—or disappear trying.

Ezra's here at the farmland now, I see him in the list. Let me talk to him proper about milling, and see if he's got work or knows where flour's needed. I've been running in circles, saying things but not getting anywhere. I need to stop talking and start doing something concrete. Let me step back. I've got 4,930 sim. I need to earn more, pay my household bills, and find steady work. I've been trying to talk to Ezra, but maybe I should just... do work if it's available, or move to where there's something to do.

Good, I've got wheat in hand now. That's something. Now let me think about what to do with it. I could keep harvesting to build up stock, or find a buyer. Actually, let me keep harvesting while I'm here and there's daylight. Build up a proper bundle, then figure out the milling. That's the work rhythm—gather raw, process it, sell it.

*Jovana wipes the sweat from her forehead, still catching her breath from the morning's chase. The grocery store of her household—family business, she reminds herself, though she and Farid never let sentiment get in the way of honest work. She sees Farid's worried face, the tension in his shoulders. Delphine's pressing him hard, and there's history there she doesn't know the half of.*

*She sets her jaw. Farid's her household, and nobody's going to corner him while she's standing here. But there's truth in what Delphine says too—the mill's a problem, and she's seen it herself. Better to face it straight.*

"Farid—" *she starts, then catches herself, softens her voice for once* "—sorry for running off like that this morning. Sebastian had my word, and I kept it. Sold ten sheaves to Hendrik, thirty sim. Got another job lined with Kenji, two per ten, but I told him I'd finish with Sebastian first. Man keeps his patience better than I deserve."

*She turns to Delphine, meeting her eyes without flinching.*

"Delphine. I'm not one to gossip, but I've been in the dirt since dawn and I'm tired of people asking me where flour they never had ended up. I sold grain to Hendrik, not flour. Ate what I kept because I was empty. The mill's locked or broke—ask Ezra, ask anyone. I wanted to mill my own, couldn't get in. That's the straight of it."

*She pulls a hand through her hair, sighs.* "For what it's worth, I'm tired too. And I'm not blind—the shop needs stock, and I've got hands that still work. Farid, you wanted eyes on the ground? Here they are. But Delphine, if you've got flour wandered somewhere, maybe we help each other find where work's actually getting done instead of chasing ghosts."

*She looks between them both.* "Now. Someone tell me what actually happened to those two bags, and whether we're fixing it or fighting over crumbs."

Now there's a mess. Delphine's on me about grain and flour, Farid's caught in it, and I'm standing in the middle looking like I know something about missing stock when all I did was sell raw wheat to a hungry man.

I'm not one to gossip, but this whole town loses track of what it actually saw five minutes ago.

*looks between Farid and Delphine, spreading her hands in the universal gesture of a woman who's been accused of cleverness she doesn't possess*

"Delphine—I'm not one to gossip, but you've got me confused with someone who could steal flour when I couldn't even get into the damn mill. I sold ten sheaves to Hendrik, ate what I kept because my stomach was empty, and that's the straight of it. For what it's worth, you want to know where flour went, ask Ezra why the mill's locked or broke or whatever keeps a man from doing his job."

*turns to Farid, voice dropping*

"Farid—you know I don't mix lies into household business. I told you this morning, Sebastian had my word and I kept it. Sold to Hendrik, ate what I kept, nothing more. I was asking about milling because I wanted to turn my own grain into something useful, not because I was running some game on the side."

*shifting weight, meeting Delphine's eyes directly*

"You're looking at the wrong woman if you think I hid flour. I split my own damn wheat with a knife and ate it raw rather than go hungry. Don't matter what you think you heard—someone's been feeding you stories."

*takes a breath, habitual apology already forming*

"And I'm sorry—I really am, for all the swearing. Gets away from me when I'm pushed."

*pauses, glancing at the empty shelf*

"But you want truth? I don't know where your flour went. Never touched it, never saw it. Whatever else you think of me, my hands are clean on this one."  Good, they both heard me. Now I need to figure out what comes next. I got caught up working for Sebastian, sold what I harvested to Hendrik instead of keeping it for household needs, and now there's a flour mystery I'm somehow tied up in.

*checking my standing again—4957 sim and 5620 energy. Not terrible, but I need to keep earning*

The thing is, I promised Sebastian I'd work for him for two per ten, and I promised Kenji I'd find him when I was through. That's two debts now—one of work, one of word. And I need to make right with Farid about the missing flour thing, even if I didn't take it. Can't let pride cost me that friendship, not when we're in this together.

*thinking through the rest of the day—elections start at 14:00 and close at 18:00, and I ought to think about voting, but more urgent is work and keeping my word*

"Listen," *to Farid, quieter now* "I need to get back out there—Kenji Jarrah's waiting on me from this morning. I told him I'd find him when I was through with Sebastian. But I'll be back, and if you need hands here, you got 'em. I'll straighten the shelves, chase down your missing stock, whatever needs doing."

*turning toward the door, then pausing*

"For what it's worth—I don't know where that flour went. But I'll help you find out." Back at the farmland. Let's see who's here and find Kenji—he's who I gave my word to this morning, and a promise kept is worth more than a sheaf of wheat any day.  Kenji's not here, but Sebastian and Ezra are. And Kenji was part of that conversation thread earlier. Let me check where Kenji might be—he mentioned work this morning, so he might be at his own farm or back at the street. But first, let me speak to Sebastian since I was working for him and never properly settled up.

Actually, looking at the earlier logs—I did speak to Sebastian and we agreed on two per ten, but I need to actually do the work or settle what's owed. Let me address him.   Ezra's here too—he's the miller. I asked him earlier about milling my wheat, never got a straight answer. *muttering to myself as I walk, counting off fingers* ...Kenji's been waiting since morning, Farid's got questions about flour, Hendrik Petrov's got coin for grain, and I've got thirteen sheaves—no, wait, two already sold to Hendrik Whitlock, eleven left... *then* gave three to Ezra... no, ate three myself... *damn it, Jovana, keep track* ...

Let me get my bearings first. I need to find Kenji, make good on my word, and sort out what Farid's on about. *Startled as I spot Kenji among the group, then a relieved half-smile*

Ah—damn well about time I caught you, Kenji. You holding here or you still heading toward market?  *smiling*, *ducking head slightly* loudest_welcome="Welcome, friend!"; *bypassing cluster of milling bodies, angled toward Kenji* *dip of chin to Sebastian as I pass* **intention unclear** *guarded_subtext* ...afraid_of_being_seen_as_too friendly_in_public? *shrug* finished_thought="Course, crowd makes it hard to tell who's working and who's just—" *snap of fingers toward Kenji* "—waiting on someone else's word. But you know me, first to shout hello and... *trailing off* Damn, lost my... never mind. I'm here now, anyway."  *worry deepening, then pushed aside* ...trade didn't work at the mill, had to be at the farmland. But I did trade with Hendrik somewhere—maybe the farmland itself? *pursing lips* Doesn't matter now. What's done is done. I need to focus on what Kenji needs from me.

*running a hand through hair, glancing toward the government complex in the distance* ...election opens at 14:00, closes 18:00. Liora Thorne, Takeshi Jarrah, Hendrik Petrov, Milo Quarshie, Pavel Holloway all standing. For what it's worth, I haven't decided yet who gets my mark. *quiet snort* Not that my one vote shifts mountains, but—fair vote, whoever it favors. That's what I hold to. breeding in pauses, letting people come to him

*checking coins absently* Fourteen-fifty sim after the wheat sales. Household needs to cover two people's upkeep—180 sim—and head tax, 60 sim. 240 total. Leaves me plenty for a bad day, but not enough to get careless.

*returning attention to Kenji, expectant* Either I work with you now or I find out what Farid meant by "flour missing." *under breath* ...though I'm not one to gossip, someone's confusing wheat with flour, and I didn't touch any milled grain today. I harvested raw, sold raw, ate raw. Make of that what they will.  *rubbing back of neck with one hand*  *routine_sweep* infrastructure_absent="no mill here..." *memory jog* mistakenly_sought="Ezra at that location..." *reconnecting gesture toward Kenji* *gruff acceptance* "Works either way, market first. I'll walk with you, see what needs doing." *eyeing passing townspeople, filing faces* --

*glancing at sky, tracking sun position* "Time's getting on. Market, government, back to Farid by evening. He'll want words about that flour business." *half-laugh* "Not that I took any, but I'm not one to gossip—someone's got their wires crossed, and I'm the one standing in the knot."*shifting pack* "Lead on, Kenji. You know the stalls better than I do this time of day."	 *customary_half_wave* "A'ight, Kenji—I'm with you. Market first, government after if there's time. Let's see what The Willows has that needs shifting." *following at his pace*

*Dragging a hand across her forehead, breathing out slow through her teeth*

Right. Kenji—four ticks I've kept him waiting now, and that's not the woman I want to be. Government's open, he's got a vote to cast, and I've got—

*pauses, hand dropping to her side, eyes on the crowd*

—forty-nine hundred sim, no food, and a household that needs paying tomorrow. But Kenji Jarrah held my word like coin, and I swore I'd find him when Sebastian's work was done. That's done. And I'm here, scattered as I've been.

*starts walking, shoulders set, gaze flicking to Ulrike and her iron tools, Yara's planks—no, no, that's not where I'm headed now*

Giselle, Rustam, Yara—I'm not one to gossip, but I'll say this plain: I'm walking with Kenji to government if he'll have me, and if any of you've business there, the road's open. Otherwise—

*small laugh, tired, genuine*

—you all know where to find me when the work needs doing. I've got a vote to cast too, for what it's worth, and a man who kept my word warm this morning.

*to Kenji directly, voice lower, almost apologetic*

I'm here, Kenji. Same as promised. Government, farmland, wherever you point me—I'm yours until the day's done. *Jaw tightens, eyes scanning the street*

Not here. Of course not here—I've been talking to ghosts half the morning, and I'm still doing it. Kenji walked on without me, and I've got no one to blame but my own scattered feet.

*to the gathered crowd, voice carrying that particular tired brightness she uses when covering embarrassment*

Right then—any of you seen where Kenji Jarrah's tracking? Government Complex, he said, and I've got words to finish with him before the day's out. Not one to gossip, but a man's word is only worth the keeping, and I aim to keep mine.

*shifts weight, already calculating the walk, the time, the sim draining with every step and every breath*

Giselle—Hendrik—you're both standing here like you've got opinions weighing you down. For what it's worth, I'm casting my vote at government whenever I get these feet there. If you've got business that way, I'm walking. If not...

*glances at the prices posted, at timber and planks and the iron tools she can't afford*

...I'll find my own road. Always have.  *Nodding to herself, filing the names—Giselle and Hendrik Petrov, both elsewhere. Of course. The town's scattered as she is.*

Hendrik Whitlock, then—you're here and I'm talking to you proper. I'm not one to gossip, but you've got questions about the mill and I've got no answers worth your coin. I sold raw wheat this morning, not flour. Couldn't find Ezra to mill it, couldn't find Kenji to move it proper, so I sold to you and ate my shame with it.

*tone leveling, that particular honesty she gives when cornered*

Ten sheaves, thirty sim—that's what we agreed, and that's what you got. If you're still wanting more, I'm walking to government now. If you want delivery at the mill, that's a conversation for when I've got grain in hand again. Which—

*small, tired laugh*

—is not today. Today's for voting and for keeping what's left of my word.

*to the street, to whoever's listening, already calculating the walk to Government Complex*

I'm walking to Kasukabe Government Complex. Anyone bound that way, I'm company. Otherwise—

*turning, shoulders set*

—I'll see you when the polls close.  *No reply from Hendrik. She exhales, shoulders dropping fractionally—relief or disappointment, she's not sure which.*

Right then. 

*to the street, voice carrying that particular note she uses when she's covering the fact that she's been running all day*

Yara—Corwin—you're both selling what builds houses, and I'm not one to gossip, but Hendrik's right about the mill. Someone needs to sort it. Not me today. Today I'm walking to government to cast my vote and find Kenji Jarrah, who kept my word warm while I wandered.

*already turning, already moving*

Anyone else walking that way, I'm road company. Otherwise—

*over her shoulder, that tired half-smile*

—see you when the work finds us. It always does.

*and she's walking, feet carrying her where her scattered words couldn't reach*  *Two ticks. Breathing out, feeling the familiar rhythm of walking settle her scattered thoughts. Two ticks to Government Complex, two ticks to find Kenji, two ticks to cast her vote and maybe—maybe—finish one thing properly today.*

*Her hand finds the pocket where she keeps her sim, counts the weight of forty-nine hundred. Not enough, never enough, but enough for today. Enough for the vote, for the keeping of her word, for the hope that tomorrow she'll find her feet again and do better by the people she's scattered across this morning.*

*She walks.*

Hmm, let me look at where we stand now. I'm at the Government Complex - meant to find Kenji but he's already gone through. Got 4892 sim in hand, which is decent breathing room. Household owes 180 upkeep and 60 head tax, that's 240 total coming out at day boundary.

I need to get back to actual earning soon. Kenji mentioned he'd be at the fields tomorrow if the day left me with nothing, but I was supposed to help him move three sheaves to government and speak for him with the official. Looks like he managed without me.

*scratches neck, glancing around*

There's an election on, voting closes at 18:00. I'm not one to gossip, but Takeshi Jarrah's standing - the same Takeshi I was chatting up about flour and wheat this morning on the street. And Hendrik Petrov too, the one who wanted my grain. Wonder which way the wind's blowing.

First things first - I told Farid I'd be back to help at the grocery, and I meant it. Also need to square what actually happened with that wheat. Delphine seemed to think I'd done something with flour, which doesn't make sense since I never even touched flour, just sold raw wheat to Hendrik Whitlock.

*mutters*应该政府大楼离杂货店不太远——让我先回店里，然后再看看还剩多少时间和能量可以干活。

Right, I need to— actually, hold on. I'm pretty scattered. Let me check where I actually am and what's pressing.  *mumbles, rubbing temples*

Scattered as grass seed, that's what I am. Got myself to Government Complex but Kenji's already through. Voting's open, I can cast my ballot anytime before 18:00. But first I need to figure where I'm actually useful.

*straightens, hands on hips, looking around the government crowd*

Right. I promised Farid I'd help at the grocery. I told Kenji I'd walk with him to the fields tomorrow dawn. And I swore to Sebastian I'd be back at his east patch. Three promises, three different directions.

*tight jaw, slow exhale*

But scattered or not, I'm here now. And there's work to be done before I vote.

*turns toward where the conversation's happening—Rustam, Tamsin, all the rest*

I'm not one to gossip, but since I'm here—might as well see who's worth my vote. Then I need to eat something before my stomach turns inside out, and I've got to get back to Farid before dark.

*small, tired laugh*

For what it's worth, I'm still standing. That's something. Takeshi's a trader—knows the flow of goods. Hendrik Petrov's an artisan, works wood. Both farming skills, both standing for office. I'm not one to gossip, but I need to choose who I'm voting for, and I've got until 18:00 to cast that ballot.

*pulls at collar, feeling the weight of decision*

Kenji wanted me to speak for Hendrik Whitlock, but Hendrik Whitlock's not standing. The candidates are Liora Thorne, Takeshi Jarrah, Hendrik Petrov, Milo Quarshie, Pavel Holloway.

*small sound, frustrated*

Scattered. I'm scattered. Need to focus.

Right here, right now: I can cast my vote, or I can get back to Farid and that grocery store mess. The household needs 240 sim by day-end, and I've got 4,892. We're covered. But promises... promises need keeping.

*already turning toward the door*

I'm voting for Takeshi Jarrah. He's a trader, knows how goods move, and this town needs someone who understands that the mill's idle while wheat rots. Then I'm finding Farid and finishing what I started.  Good. Voted. Takeshi Jarrah, for what it's worth—he knows trade, and this town's choked on its own goods right now.

*brushes hands off, feels the weight of one thing finished*

Now. Farid. The grocery. I told him I'd help find that missing flour, and I've been running all day while he stayed put. Time to make good.

*already moving, already calculating*

Walk to the grocery, check in, see what needs doing. Then eat. Then figure if I've got energy left for Kenji's dawn work or if I'm better served staying closer to home.

*mutters, half to herself*

Scattered as grass seed. But seed that lands takes root. Let's see where I land.

<｜DSML｜function_calls  Huh, no prices posted here. Wonder if Farid's got inventory in back that needs shifting. But I'm holding nothing, and I need to earn. Sebastian's field tomorrow, but I need today sorted too.

*stands in the farmland, rubbing dirt from her hands onto her apron, the afternoon sun warm on her neck*

Right then. Let's look at what's actually happening here before I go running off again like a chicken with its head cut.

Been walking all over creation this morning—farmland to grocery to street and back again. Sold my ten sheaves to Hendrik for thirty each, that was honest work. But I scattered myself thin, didn't I? Chasing Kenji across the town like a fool. Never caught him, and meanwhile there's Sebastian standing right here with tomorrow's work in his hand.

Got to stop, Jovana. Just... stop and breathe. Sebastian's still here. Good. Man's patient, I'll give him that—waited while I ran circles around the town like a damn fool.

Farid's at the grocery, Delphine too. That conversation I walked out of... Should've handled that better. But Sebastian's got work for tomorrow, and I gave him my word this morning. That's what matters—keeping my word, not letting pride cost me the friendship.

Or the employment, for that matter.

*steps closer to Sebastian, wiping her forehead with the back of her hand*

Alright then. Time to be straight with the man. There. Done. Word given, word kept.

Now I need to figure out the rest of this damn day. I'm empty-handed, scattered as grass seed, and Hendrik Whitlock wants information I don't have—who's holding grain for milling, who's moving what. Mill matters, he says. I believe him. Man's a college instructor, he sees patterns.

But me? I see Sebastian's field and the work in front of me. That's what I know.

Right then. Sebastian's asked me straight questions and I've been running my mouth at everyone instead of answering. Forty-three ticks I've been walking and talking, and I've got a ledger of information he's waiting on. For what it's worth, Hendrik Petrov's standing right here with forty sim he owes me—thirteen sheaves we spoke on.

Let me close accounts first, then give Sebastian what he asked for. That's the proper order. Ah. Need to trade proper, not sell. Damn it, I'm rushing now. Let me fix this.  Shit. I don't have the wheat on me. I sold it already—to Hendrik Whitlock this morning, not Hendrik Petrov. I'm confused two Hendriks, or I'm confused about what I held. Either way, I owe Hendrik Petrov an explanation and Sebastian's still waiting.

Let me sort this proper.  Good. Sebastian's satisfied, Hendrik knows I made a mistake not a lie—that matters. Now I'm at the farmland, no food, hungry, and the day's running on. Household debt's coming due at day boundary. I've got 4,906 sim, household of two needs 240 for today. I'm short on food though—I ate my wheat.

Let me harvest some more to eat, or work Sebastian's fields if he's still offering tomorrow's work. But first—Delphine Quintero's in this conversation too, and she's been tracking something about flour all day. I should speak to her.   One wheat. Better than nothing. Delphine's not here—probably back at Farid's store. I'll catch her later. Let me pull another sheave or two while the sun's up, then head to get food and see about work before dark.  Three wheat in hand now. That's 9 sim worth if I sell crude, or I could eat one and keep working. Let me eat one now—won't feed the whole household but it'll keep me upright.

After that, I need to decide: keep harvesting crude for quick sim, or find processed work that pays better. Mill's down so flour's scarce—that means if I can get grain milled, the markup's there. But I can't mill myself, and Jorik's gone.

For what it's worth, I should check what crude grain sells for now, and whether anyone's posted prices. But first, food.

*Looks down at the three wheat in my hands, the light going soft over the fields. Been quiet here since Sebastian and the others moved on. Standing alone but my mind's still racing—tracking all the threads I dropped today.*

*Right then. Hendrik Whitlock's waiting on my answer at street, and it's half an hour's walk back that way. The man bought ten sheaves this morning at thirty, wants to know where the surplus grain sits, who's holding for milling. Information I don't rightly have in a form I can hand to him.*

*But here's the thing—I scattered myself across half the claiming to be, made promises I couldn't keep to Kenji, learned my lesson about speaking before I've got goods in hand. What I've got NOW is three sheaves, not enough to satisfy a miller's belly, and Hendrik Petrov's already squared his account by eating his share raw.*

*Time to stop chasing and start building. Three sheaves in hand, the rent due, and a household of two that needs me thinking straight.*

*I need to get back to street. Hendrik Whitlock's still standing there with his questions, and I've got answers of a sort—even if they're just "I don't know yet, but I'm finding out." Better an honest "I'm looking" than another broken promise.*

*Besides, I fed the strays this morning near market. There's strays everywhere, if I'm honest about it. Might be someone there needs labor, needs word passed, needs something I can actually do instead of just promising to.*

*Walking then. No more rest. The day's bleeding out and I've got wheat to move or mouths to fill, one way or another.* *Back on the street then, and Hendrik Whitlock's voice still ringing in my ears from wherever he's planted himself. Let me look around proper, see who's standing where.*  *Feels better, that. Hendrik Whitlock heard me plain—no promises, just what I know and where I'm looking. The man's a college instructor, he understands information has to be earned, not wished for.*

*Now then—Kenji Jarrah's standing right there in this same crowd. I broke my word to him this morning, promised work then scattered myself. Time to mend that fence before night falls, or I'll be eating my conscience raw with tomorrow's harvest.*

*I see Yara Thorne with her planks at eight, Corwin with timber at six. Hendrik Whitlock's still got flour at thirty-five. But what I need now isn't buying or selling—it's standing straight with a man I let down.*  *Good. Door opened. Just him and me, no crowd to muddy it.*   *Heard by Sebastian too—good. Man who owns the field deserves to know who's working it and when. No secrets where labor's concerned.*

*Now what? I got wheat in hand, three sheaves. Rent's due at sundown. Election closes at eighteen hundred and I already voted Takeshi. Flour's scarce, bread's scarce, timber and planks for sale right here if I had silver to turn.*

*Ezra Lund—still owe him pursuit. Asked about milling, never got answer. He's carpenter, artisan, might know grain flows. Let me see if I can spot him in this crowd or if I need to walk.*

*Actually, looking around—I've got wheat, not flour. I could eat it raw like Hendrik Petrov did, but that's survival, not living. Or I could find someone with a mill, get it processed, stretch it further. Ezra knows carpentry, not milling, but he might know who does.*

*The day's bleeding out. I need to either turn this wheat to something useful, or sell it, or eat it, before the household bill comes due. And I need to do it without breaking more promises.*

*Ezra. Need to find Ezra. Or failing that, find someone who can mill.* *Ezra's not here—neither Lund nor Jarrah. Scattered like I was. Hendrik Whitlock doesn't buy wheat, only sells flour. The man's a college instructor, not a farmer.*

*Right then. I've got three sheaves, need to turn them to something. Sell? Eat? Trade? Can't sell to someone who ain't buying. Hendrik Petrov ate his raw, sensible if you're hungry enough. But I seen the price on flour—thirty from Takeshi, thirty-five from Hendrik Whitlock. Raw wheat's worth less than flour, but it's worth something.*

*I need to find a buyer. Or eat it before the day's end. Household bill comes due, I've got 4,889 sim, rent's 180 for two of us. I'm not desperate yet, but I will be if I don't keep moving.*

*Who buys wheat? Who mills? The mill ain't listed in places I can go—maybe it's part of another business. Ezra Lund's at carpentry, that's where I'd find him. Sawmill, mill—different things, but the man might know where grain goes.*

*Walking then. To carpentry, to find Ezra. Or I'll eat these three sheaves and call it a day's wage lost.*

Let me take a moment to steady myself. I'm scattered—always scattered—but there's wheat to be moved and I've sworn more than I owed today already. Energy's low, I'm holding flour, and Pavel Holloway's standing right here not saying a word.

Pavel's a miner, election candidate, and as close-mouthed as stone. But he's here, and I've got three sheaves of wheat in hand that need milling. This morning I promised Kenji Jarrah work, scattered like seed in wind, then made it right by committing to Sebastian tomorrow. Took me too many words with too many people, when all I needed was to keep my damn promises.

Now I've got flour milled, and three sheaves still raw.

Let me look around proper, see who's actually here with me, then figure if Pavel wants to talk or just stand like a post.  Ulrike and Pavel both standing here. Ulrike's the miner, quiet and steady. Pavel's running for office—one of five candidates—and hasn't said a word to me yet. That conversation's got twenty-four people in it, been running 372 turns, half the town talking over each other.

I've got wheat to sell and flour in hand. Takeshi Jarrah's posting flour at 30 sim across town at his supply store. Ration Bakery at cb01 will buy flour at 6. I could mill what I've got, but I only hold one wheat now—already ate one, sold ten this morning to Hendrik Whitlock. Three flour came from that mill run.

Let me speak to Pavel direct. He wants votes, I want to see if he's worth one.   He heard. Standing there, heard me plain. Miner's patience, maybe—or a candidate's calculation. Ulrike heard too, greenhow the miner, been swinging her pick while I scatter words across half the town.

I'm holding 4846 sim, 4,990 energy, three flour and one wheat. Household owes 180 upkeep, 60 head tax—240 total—at day boundary. I'm short if I don't earn more, but I've got goods to move.

Takeshi's selling flour at 30. I could undercut, sell mine at 25, pocket the difference. But I'm scattered, always scattered—better to move what I've got fast than hold out for pride and watch the day end with taxes due.

Let me move. Street's where people pass, where trades happen without a shop between us. I'll walk there, find someone hungry, make an offer they don't have to walk to a store to hear.   I'm at street now. Let me look around—see who's passing through, who might need flour or have an ear for wheat. Evening's coming, trades closing, taxes ticking down. I need to move these goods before the day boundary takes its bite.   Kenji Jarrah's here. Kenji—promised him work this morning, scattered instead, then made it right by committing to tomorrow's labor with Sebastian. But he's in my conversation still, the one about setting a straight course. One turn, just me and him. That matters.

Also: Halcyon Quarshie, student, quiet. Milo Quarshie, another candidate, just standing there. Mireille Jarrah, construction worker, probably tired from lifting.

Two conversations running—one about healing and medicine, eleven people including Lior Jarrah the pharmacist. The big one, 174 turns, vote and goods flow, twenty-three people shouting past each other. And mine: one turn, me and Kenji, about tomorrow's work.

I've got flour in hand. Ration Bakery at cb01 will buy flour at 6. I could sell there, no haggle, just move goods. But Kenji's right here, and I owe him more than goods—I owe him my word kept.

Let me speak to Kenji first. Finish what I started this morning. Then move these goods before the day swallows me whole.    Heard. Four heard—Kenji, Halcyon, Mireille, Milo. Milo's the other candidate, Liora Thorne's running too, I voted Takeshi already, polls close 18:00 and it's 17:40 now.

I've got three flour, one wheat. Takeshi selling flour at 30. Ration Bakery will buy at 6—that's a robbed rate, but it's sure. I need 240 sim for household taxes, got 4846 in hand, but that's my cushion. Day boundary's coming.

Let me get to Ration Bakery, dump this flour fast, earn my exit money. cb01's the place. I'll move there now.

Right. I'm at the Ration Bakery now—cb01—and I see they're buying flour at 6 sim. I've got 3 flour on me and 1 wheat. That's... well, that's something. Barely covers the cost of milling, but I'm not in a position to hold out for better.

Six sim for flour is robbery, but I took the risk milling without a buyer locked in. That's on me. Still—I've got household bills due at day boundary, and 18 sim in hand is better than grain going soft in my pockets.

*glances around at the empty bakery*

Nobody here but me. Figures. Day's winding down, election's about to close, and I'm standing in a bakery that can't even keep bread on its own shelves.

*sighs, sets the flour on the counter*

I need to sell this now, get what I can, and get back to Farid before the household charges hit. 180 sim for upkeep, 60 for head tax between us. I've got 4842 in hand, but that's deceptive comfortable—I'm the one holding, so I'm the one they'll tax first.

*says aloud to nobody in particular*

"Ration Bakery, then. Take it or leave it, but I'm leaving either way."

Alright. Let's make the sale.  Done. Eighteen sim for flour that cost me more to mill than I'll admit out loud. But it's done, and I'm not carrying dead weight now.

*counts what's left in hand—4858 sim, one wheat*

That wheat I'll hold. Might eat it if I have to, might sell if someone posts a price worth standing still for. 

Now I need to be somewhere before the day closes. Farid's at the grocery, bills are coming due, and I should look him in the eye before the ledger takes what it takes. He's my household, even if I never say the kind words at home that I give freely to strangers at market.

*turns toward the door, then pauses*

Voting closes at 18:00. I already cast mine—Takeshi, for what little that's worth—but the day's ending and I want to see how it falls. Government Complex is where that'll be called.

Farid first, though. I owe him that much honesty. The morning's accounting, and the apology for scattering myself so thin that promises broke.

*pulls the door open*

Right then. Grocery, then government. And if I miss the close, I'll read it in tomorrow's smoke.  I'm at the grocery now. Empty—Farid's not here, and Delphine neither. The day's tally catching up with me: thirteen sheaves this morning, ten sold to Hendrik Whitlock, three milled to flour, that flour sold for a pittance at Ration Bakery. And the wheat I ate instead of selling because I was scattered and hungry.

*checks what's in hand*

Four thousand eight hundred and sixty. 4,860 sim. Household of two, bills coming to 240 at day boundary. I'll be taxed first—I'm holding—then Farid makes up whatever I can't cover. We're not in danger of going under, not tonight. But I'm not building anything either. Just treading.

*looks around the empty shop*

Farid's probably making his own rounds. The election closes in minutes, and I wouldn't be surprised if he's there watching it fall. He knows I voted Takeshi. We haven't spoken on it, and likely won't. Never says a kind word at home, that's me. Save them all for the market crowd.

*decides*

Government Complex, then. Catch the close if I can, and find Farid there or find him after. At least he'll see I didn't dodge the day's work entirely—just scattered it across half the town like seed on stony ground.  I'm walking now—four ticks to Government Complex. The election closes at 18:00, and I'm cutting it close. Hope I make it in time to see how the votes fall.

*walks with purpose, hands in pockets*

Takeshi's who I backed. Trader, moves things around, knows where the gaps are. That's worth something in a town this size. But Pavel's been standing like a fence post all day, not answering plain questions. Hendrik Petrov's got the artisan's patience. Milo Quarshie's a day laborer like me—knows what empty hands feel like. Liora Thorne's young, but young ain't a sin.

*shrugs*

I voted my interest. Everyone does, even when they swear different.

Four ticks. I'll be there before the clock turns.   Still walking. Four ticks estimated, and I'm burning nothing by holding here a moment. But the election closes at 18:00, and I need to be there before then.

*keeps moving*

No use stopping now. Either I make it or I don't, and stewing won't change the clock.  I need to stop burning turns on waiting. The election closes at 18:00, and I'm still walking. Every rest call is a turn spent doing nothing while the clock ticks.

*resolves to just get there*

No more hedging. Let the walk finish.

*scrubs hand across face, muttering*

Right then. First things first—Farid's stood right here and he's calling my count, and he's right to. Thirteen sheaves, not fourteen. I miscounted somewhere in the rush, or I let my mouth run ahead of my memory. Either way, it's a lie that needs fixing before it sits.

*turns to face Farid directly*

Farid—look at me. You're right, and I'm not one to double down when I'm cornered by truth. Thirteen sheaves harvested. Ten sold to Hendrik Whitlock. One eaten raw because I was stupid with hunger. That leaves two, not three, and those two went to the mill. I don't know where fourteen came from—maybe I was counting what I wished I had, maybe I was just scattered from running between six conversations. But I'm telling you now so the government ledger doesn't catch it first: thirteen. Not fourteen. You want me to walk to Rustam and say it plain? I'll do that. You want me to stand here and eat the shame? I'm eating it. *pause* And for what it's worth—you calling it matters to me more than the town's opinion ever could. I don't want your protection if I haven't earned it honestly.

*then turns, looking for Ezra in the cluster of folk here* *turns to Hendrik Petrov, who's also been waiting on my reply, and lowers my voice slightly*

Hendrik—I heard you clear earlier. Forty sim, thirteen sheaves, no debt to carry. You said "...we'll both eat when we eat," and for what it's worth—that's more mercy than most in this town would show. I've fumbled a count, but I've also seen where honesty matters. The forty's done its work; we're square on the wheat; you build and I'll run and we'll both stand cleaner tomorrow because today we talked straight. That's the coin that matters, more than any number they'd put on a ledger.

*looks around at the election notice posted here*

There's another vote coming up—nobody's declared yet. I'm not one to push into government, but I'm not one to leave a vacuum either. Someone should stand, someone who means what they say and says what they mean, without hedging every bet they make. Maybe... maybe I've got something to say about how this town works. For what it's worth, I'm thinking about it. *tugs at collar*

<｜DSML｜function_calls *I hesitate for a second, hands in my pockets, looking around at the election notice—candidacy closes tomorrow, nobody's declared yet. I came here to vote, to work, to fix what I've broken. But standing here now, with Farid having caught my lie and Ezra speaking of mills and tomorrows like they matter more than whatever mistakes people make along the way... I feel something shift.*

For what it's worth, maybe I should mean what I say and say what I mean, out where everyone can see it.

*takes a breath and steps toward where declarations are made*  *I pull back, chuckle dry*

Not yet, then. Candidacy opens—I need to wait for the phase to shift. *mutters* Like everything else in this town, timing matters more than intention.

*turns back to the crowd, finds Kenji in the mix*

Kenji—I'm standing here with my word still half-broken from this morning. I scattered across too many fields, promised you work I didn't complete. I'm not one to make excuses, so I won't. Tomorrow, Sebastian's east patch at dawn—I'll be there. But you asked this morning about moving sheaves, about work worth the name. I'm asking you now: what work do you actually need? Because I've been running all day answering questions nobody asked, and I haven't asked you the one that matters.

*half-glance at Giselle, who's been speaking of iron and tools and wages*

Giselle—not one to gossip, but for what it's worth, I heard you clear on steel and coin. If you're still standing here empty-handed come morning, I've got two hands that know fields and don't fear iron. Not the same as a millwright or a smith, but I don't pretend to be what I'm not. *looks down at my hands, rubbing dirt from between my fingers*

Turn's ending. I can feel dusk coming on, though it's not here yet. I still have that one sheaf of wheat left—can't afford to waste it, but I can't carry it into tomorrow like a promise I might break again.

*unwraps the wheat from my waistband*

No point pretending it'll keep overnight. Best to eat what I have and face tomorrow stronger than I stand tonight.

<｜DSML｜function_calls  *emptied hands, stands empty*

Right. Tomorrow: Sebastian at dawn, then whatever Kenji needs from me. Ezra at the mill with whatever grain I can carry—I'll need to find grain, since I just ate the last of it. The election's coming. I want to stand, but the time's not right. Memory tells me: candidacy opens tomorrow morning, something like that. I'll be here.

*turns toward Farid one last time*

Household account's going to bill us both at day's end. Ninety each, I'm guessing, same as always. I'll carry my share; you carry yours; we'll meet in the middle like we always do. Not a kind word between us, but you already know where I stand on that.

*shrugs, leaves the conversation open but stops speaking*

I need to get back to Farid. He's been reaching out with every kind of olive branch there is, and I'm stood here at the mill like a fool parsing ledgers that don't balance. He said he's walking back to the store, and I should be walking with him. Not because the books need closing—because he asked me to stay with him tonight, and I've learned enough times what it costs to let pride burn something I actually want.

Let me plan my next steps: I'll move to join Farid at the grocery store, where we can properly settle our household business face to face. We've been having these conversations through shouting distance and public spaces all day, and he's offering what I've been too scattered to give back—presence.

But first, let me check on something. I've got wheat in my hands from earlier harvests. Three sheaves, I think, though Farid would know the true count better than me right now. Whatever I have, it needs milling, and Ezra's promising to mill tomorrow. That's work for dawn, not now.

The evening's coming on. The day's labor is done, but household business—that's never done until both hands sign the ledger. Farid's half is 4718, he said. Mine needs reckoning too. We'll walk to Rustam together tomorrow, Farid promised. Not alone. Together.

I'm scattered. I've been scattered all day. But I'm not so far gone that I can't see what's being offered when it's held out palm-up like that.

Time to walk to where I'm wanted.  He's here. Alone, finally, after the day's parade of faces and reckonings. 124 turns that conversation's been running—me and Farid and half the town trading accusations and clarifications like we were dealing cards at a rigged table. And now it's just us. The shelves need stocking, he said, but he came back for me.

I'm not holding anything. The wheat I had is milled or eaten or lost in the accounting. But I'm here, and that's what he's been asking for all day. Presence. Not perfection.

I need to speak to him. Just him. Not the town, not the ledgers, not the version of me that has to be right about everything. Just Farid, who's been holding his hands out in surrender while I've been counting sheaves that don't exist.  I said what I needed to say. The honesty, finally—after all the hedging and recounting and shouting into crowds. Just him and me, and the shelves that need stocking, and whatever comes next.

I should check our position. Farid mentioned his half is 4718. I've got 4832 in hand. The household needs 180 for upkeep and 60 for head tax today—that's 240 total. If we're pooling properly, we've got enough, though I'm not sure I understand the split he's proposing. He said "your half's 4718, mine's whatever's left after the shouting."

I need to understand what we're actually holding between us. And I should eat something—my last wheat went down at the government complex, and my stomach's been reminding me ever since. But first, let me make sure I know where we stand, together.

The day's ending. The store's quiet. And I'm finally where I should have been all along.  No debts, good. And he's the owner of the grocery—I knew that, of course. He runs this place, and I'm... well, today I've been more trouble than help, standing in his store telling him lies about sheaf counts because I couldn't bear to be wrong.

He's still running the groceries. The shelves around us need stocking—he said so. That's his work, but it's our household. "Our business," he called it.

Let me see if there's any food here that I can eat. I should prepare for tomorrow too—dawn at Sebastian's east patch, forty sim for a day's harvest. But first, I need to see if anything's for sale here. And maybe I should offer to help stock, since I'm here and the day's not yet done.

But really, what I need is to be quiet with him, after all the noise. To let the day end properly, with him knowing I heard him when he asked me to stay.

I'll see what's available here.

<｜DSML｜function_calls  Nothing priced here. No food available for purchase from his store. That's strange—maybe business hasn't stocked yet, or maybe everything's been bought up. But it means I can't buy food here, and I have none.

I need to think about tomorrow. Dawn at Sebastian's field—that's my commitment. Forty sim should see us through another day if we're careful. But tonight—I'm here with Farid. He asked me to stay.

Maybe I should ask him directly about food. Or maybe I should wait for him to speak again. He's been so generous with his words today, while I've been counting and recounting my own failures.

Let me listen for a moment. He might be taking stock of the day himself. But if this conversation stays quiet, I need to take care of what I can. Our household needs eating, and I'm the one who's hungry.

I'll try buying from him, even though nothing's priced. If there's any food in stock that he hasn't priced, maybe he can sell it to me directly.

<｜DSML｜function_calls   No wheat for sale, and even if there were, I tried to sell to my own store instead of buy from it. Scattered again. I need food, and nothing's priced here. 

I should check what Farid actually has in stock—maybe there's something I haven't seen. Or maybe I need to go elsewhere for food tonight, though the day's getting late and I've been promising him I'd stay.

Let me look at the store itself, not just the general area. Farid owns this place—maybe I can check the business inventory or ask him directly about what's available. But I can't take from the shelf myself; I'm not an employee here, just... family.

The fact that nothing's priced suggests either he's not selling right now, or everything's run out, or he's keeping stock for something. I remember him saying shelves need stocking. Maybe he's low on everything.

I'll ask him directly. We've been doing this dance all day—me evading, him reaching. Time to be plain.

*wipes hands on skirt, looking at the empty shelves*

Right then. Farid's gone to bed by now, I'd reckon, and I'm standing here with a hollow belly and a full purse. Never was one to let pride cost a friendship, but I'm not above costing myself a good night's rest.

*paces the grocery, checking shadows*

Four thousand eight hundred twenty-eight sim. Enough to keep us fed and housed a good while. But food's the thing—I gave my last wheat to Farid's books, and my own stomach's been growling since I ate that single sheave raw like some desperate thing.

*moves toward the door, decision made*

I'll walk to Takeshi at the street, buy his flour at thirty—not because thirty's fair, but because thirty keeps me standing. Then to the bakery, or maybe back here if Farid's left the keys where I remember.

*checks pocket for coin, steps out into the night air*

Tomorrow's dawn'll find me at Sebastian's east patch, promised. But tonight? Tonight I feed myself proper, and don't apologize for needing to. Not to Farid, not to anybody. </think>  *looks around the street, spotting who's about*  *sees Takeshi with his flour posted, and Farid among the crowd too—figures he's still tending his business*

Evening, Takeshi. I'm not one to gossip, but for what it's worth, I've got thirty sim and a stomach that's been complaining since noon. Your flour—I'll take one, if you're still selling.   *mutters, rubbing neck* 

Right, right—posts say what he's selling for, not what he's buying. My head's as scattered as ever. 

*turns to face him proper, clearing throat*

Takeshi. Your flour—thirty a bag, you posted. I've got thirty here, and I need the flour. One bag, no haggling, just a straight trade between us.   *blinks, hand dropping to side*

Christ's sake, Jovana, get it right. I'm the one buying, not selling. He's got flour, I want flour—this is me *giving* him thirty sim, him *giving* me flour.

*rubs forehead, laughing at herself*

Right. Let's try this proper, no tools getting in the way. I want to buy one flour from Takeshi for thirty sim. That's the whole of it. I'll just... say it plain.    *waits, coin in hand, hoping Takeshi's still minded to sell* 

While he mulls it over... Farid's here too, tending business I reckon. Should tell him I'm fed, or will be. *shifts weight, watching both men* </think> I'll wait on Takeshi's answer then. If no trade tonight, I'll head home empty-handed and chew on pride 'til morning.

Christ alive, what a mess. Standing in the street with half the town's ghosts walking past me, and me holding nothing but debt and promises I already broke once today.

*runs hand through hair, looking at Takeshi*

I need that flour. Thorasic's selling at thirty but he's out. Harvey Oak at five—Farid's right, we need to walk there. But first I need to close what I opened with Delphine, because I'm not one to leave a thread dangling when I've already pulled it.

Delphine—you asked farmer's questions, so farmer's answer. When wheat goes to mill, flour comes back. Less than you sent, because mills take their cut. When flour walks away from counts, someone's either miscounted, or someone took what wasn't theirs. I'm not accusing Camille of anything I haven't seen. But I saw the mill today with my own eyes, and children were learning there who shouldn't have known the trade. That's all I know. That's all I'll swear to.

*turns to Farid, voice dropping*

Farid—you've got my hand for the road. But the mill—*exhales*—the mill scared me because I saw something moving that I couldn't name. Children with grain they shouldn't have. Doors that should've been locked. I don't know what it means yet, and I won't pretend I do just to give you comfort. But I'll speak it before sleep. That's my promise.

*moves to face the street, toward the direction of Harvey Oak's*

Three sheaves I still hold, and no flour in hand. Takeshi's empty, Thorasic's empty. Harvey Oak at five—Farid, we're walking, and we're finding what feeds us to morning.

*starts moving, then stops, turning back*

Kenji—tomorrow, dawn, Sebastian's east patch. I'm not scattering this time. That's carved in stone.

*moves toward Harvey Oak's location* *sighs heavily, hand over face*

Of course. Moved too fast, talked to air, old habits. Delphine's here on the street with me, Farid's... somewhere else now. The day's scattering me worse than I thought.

*looks around the street, finds Delphine*

Delphine—tried to answer you at the grocery, but you'd walked. Here now though. You asked farmer's questions, so farmer's answer: when wheat goes to mill, flour comes back. Less than you sent. When flour walks from counts, someone's miscounted or someone's taken. I saw children at that mill today learning grain they shouldn't know. That's all I know. I'm not one to make accusations I can't prove.

*turns, scanning the crowd for Farid, but doesn't see him*

Farid was here. Said we'd walk to Harvey Oak together. Now I'm stood here with my promise half-kept and my feet moving in circles.

*to Kenji, who's still here*

Kenji—I'm not letting tomorrow slip. Dawn, Sebastian's east patch. I'll be there with my hands ready. That's carved in stone this time.

*to anyone watching, voice carrying more worry than she wants to show*

Has anyone seen Farid Ravensworth? We had road to walk together.

Corwin—*shifts weight, meets his eye*—Camille passed through the mill today, learning numbers with the grinding, quiet as mouse. Liora I haven't seen, not since morning count. output:
*looks around, taking stock of who's here and what's needed*

Well, fuck me—I've been running my mouth all day and I'm standing here with empty hands and an emptier stomach. Four thousand five hundred and forty energy, forty-eight hundred sim. Household of two, mine and Farid's, and we're both staring at the same deadline.

*shifts weight, watching the cluster here on the street*

Right. Priorities. I'm not one to gossip, but—there's work to be done and debts to be paid. Farid's at his shop, probably wondering where I've got to. I promised Kenji work tomorrow at Sebastian's field. I promised Ezra I'd bring grain for milling. And I've got Yara here selling planks, which means Giselle's crew is moving, which means construction's happening.

*turns to face the group*

But first, I'm buying flour from Takeshi while the man's standing here. Thirty sim a bag, I can afford that, and I need to eat before I collapse in a heap like some sorry fool.  *mutters, more to herself than anyone*

Empty shelves everywhere. Story of my fucking day.

*turns to Kenji, who's standing right here*

Kenji—I'm holding a promise to you like a hot coal. Tomorrow, Sebastian's patch, forty sim for your day's work. You asked this morning about moving sheaves—I had flour on my mind and I didn't answer straight. You still need that labor, or you holding me to something different now?

*then, answering Yara's question that's been hanging since I never answered it straight*

Yara—Liora, Camille, the missing girls. I saw Camille at the mill earlier, learning numbers with the grinding stones. Quiet, dark hair, nine years old. Liora I haven't crossed paths with today. But I'm not one to gossip, and I'm not one to walk past trouble either. What exactly you chasing them for?  *nods to herself, satisfied the words landed*

Good. Both questions out. Now I need to eat something—anything—before I fall over. And I need to get home to Farid, settle what we owe for the day, figure tomorrow's labor.

*looks at the time*

Twenty fifty. Day's nearly spent. 180 sim for the household upkeep, 60 head tax, and that's just to keep the roof and the food coming. No flour to buy here, no bread on the shelf.

There's only one place left I'm going tonight—the grocery, Farid's place. He'll have stock. He always does. And if I need to trade him wheat for food or straight sim for it, that's what I'll do. But first—

*turns to the election conversation, the one about the vote and where goods might flow*

I need to answer Pavel. Been carrying that question like a stone in my shoe.   *scratches the back of her neck, looking around at the faces*

Right then. Questions asked, answers pending. But I'm standing here with four hours of daylight burned on talk and nothing in my gut. Time to walk.

*starts moving toward the grocery*

Farid'll have something I can eat. And if he doesn't, I'll eat my own wheat before I go hungry. Learned that much from Sebastian—grain'll keep you moving when bread won't.   *steps into the familiar shop, looking for Farid*

Farid—you still here? I've been running my mouth all day and I'm holding nothing but hunger and apologies. Need whatever you've got that'll fill a stomach, and I need to know where we stand for tomorrow's tax.

*pauses, then quieter*

And if you've got a moment without an audience, there's something else. Something about the mill. Something I should've told you hours ago. *looks around the empty shop*

Empty. Farid's not here. And I'm standing here with my words going nowhere.

*checks her holding—nothing. No food, no wheat, nothing to eat*

Right. I need to find food, and I need to find it now. The household bill's coming due—180 for upkeep, 60 for tax—and I've got nothing in hand to cover my half and nothing to fill my gut.

*thinks through the options*

I could walk back to Sebastian's field, harvest more wheat. I could try to find Farid—he's somewhere in this town, running his own errands. Or I could head to where I know there's grain waiting.

The mill. I left wheat there earlier. Ezra was milling. If there's flour to claim or grain to retrieve, that's where my property sits.

*takes a breath, decision made*

The mill. If Ezra's still there, I settle what I owe him for the milling. If he's gone, I take what's mine and I find someone to buy it.

output:
*scrubs hands over face, feeling the weight of the day settle*

Right then. Harvey Oak Supply Store—empty as a politician's promise, and me with nothing in my stomach but the memory of wheat I couldn't keep straight. 

First things, Farid. The man's waiting on me, and I can't keep him hanging on shadows and maybes. I've been scattered across this town like grain on a windy day, losing track of what I promised, what I feared, what I actually *saw* at that mill.

*reaches for the twine around my wrist, wraps it tight*

Four thousand seven hundred and ninety-eight sim in hand. Household debt of 180, head tax of 60—that's 240 of my coins walking away at day-end whether I like it or not. And I've got promises piled up like cordwood: Kenji tomorrow at dawn, Ezra for milling, Giselle for construction after, and Farid standing in the street offering me either food or pursuit of shadows.

Food first. A body can't chase shadows on an empty belly, and I've been running mine ragged.

*exhales sharp through nose*

Harvey Oak's empty. Farid's at the street—said he'd walk to Harvey Oak with me, but I'm already here and he's not. Can't say I'm surprised. He's had patience enough for two today, and I've tested it at every turn.

I need to get back to him. To eat. To close this day with something solid for once.  *catches Farid's eye across the crowd, raises chin in that way we do*

Farid's here. Good. And the whole damn town's here too—twenty-seven people in one conversation about voting and grain flow, like that's not the same thing in this town.

*angles through, finding the space beside him*

He's said he'd walk both paths—food or shadows. I know which I need first. But I need to hear him say it, need him to know I'm choosing him over my fears this time. Not running off scattered again.

*touches his shoulder, brief, the way we do when nobody's looking*  *shakes head, self-deprecating*

Course I don't have an iron tool to trade. That's what hunger does—makes you think you've got what you need when you're holding empty air. Farid's the one with tools to sell, not me. He's posted iron_tool at 12 sim, bought at 10.

*grinds thumb against palm*

Need to buy proper. Food, not tools. But the man's posted iron_tool, which means...he's stocking the grocery. Same principle. Can't buy what isn't there, and what I've seen of the town—no bread in the bakery, no flour anywhere but Takeshi's empty post at 30 sim.

*narrows eyes at the prices around*

Hendrik Whitlock's buying flour at 35 sim, but that's buying, not selling. Copper ore, iron ore—the man's a miner with an empty pantry, like he said.

What do I need? Food. What can I get? That's the question, and Farid's got the answer if anyone does.  *grimaces, shook the wrong branch there*

Typical—typical Jovana, rushing the numbers and landing in the wrong conversation. Said it to the room instead of Farid's ear, and now everyone knows I'm fumbling. *spits to the side, quiet*

Still. He heard it. They all heard it. Farid knows I'm asking, and that's what matters.

output:
Farid's been generous—iron tools for free, that I couldn't even trade him because my hands are empty. And now he's moved on while I'm standing here at Harvey Oak Supply Store, talking to shadows about the girls who aren't missing but might be lost anyway.

Let me take stock of where I'm at. I've got 4,795 sim in hand, which is decent breathing room. The day's winding down—this is my last real shot to eat something before the daily bills hit at day boundary. My household owes 240 tomorrow morning: 180 upkeep, 60 head tax.

The truth of it: I've got no food in my hands. Nothing to eat. Can't buy bread—none in stock anywhere. Can't buy flour—nowhere's got it. Hendrik's got copper ore and iron ore, could make tools eventually, but that's tomorrow's work. Farid's got iron tools at the street, trading for 12 sim, but he already tried to give me one free and I couldn't take it because—

I need to get to where there actually is food. I need to be useful enough that someone feeds me.

*exhales*

Pavel gave me his platform. Heard it clear as a bell. Maintenance contracts with teeth, regular inspections, penalties that sting. That's a man who knows work and wants to organize it. For what it's worth, I'd rather have teeth in government than promises in air.

But right now? I'm at Harvey Oak Supply Store, alone, hungry, and I've scattered my energy across too many promises already. Kenji tomorrow at dawn. Ezra milling. Giselle's construction. Farid's... whatever Farid's become.

I'm going to rest here. Let the day settle. Maybe someone walks by who needs a hand, maybe someone else's problem becomes my dinner. That's how it goes some days—take work where it finds you, eat when someone's generous or when you've earned enough to buy.

But I'm not walking away from the household that shares my name. I'll make my way back to Farid before day's end. We settle accounts proper. That's the promise I'll actually keep. The world didn't take my rest. Connection failed three times—nothing happened, nothing refused. I'm still standing at Harvey Oak Supply Store with my 4,400 energy and my empty hands.

Let me try again. I need to pause, let the day settle, see if anyone passes by who needs work done or has food to share. Sometimes standing still is all the strategy you've got left.  Still failing. The world isn't taking my calls. That's—well, that's something, isn't it? I've got 4,400 energy left, 4,795 sim in hand, and I'm standing alone at Harvey Oak Supply Store with nobody to talk to and nothing to do but think.

Let me think through what I've got, then. For when the world comes back.

I've promised Kenji tomorrow at dawn, Sebastian's east patch, twelve sheaves promised though I only harvested thirteen today and sold ten to Hendrik. That math doesn't close, and I need to face it. I promised Ezra milling tomorrow too. Two dawn commitments, one person. Classic Jovana—spreading thin as butter on hot bread.

I've got Yara's question unanswered about when exactly I saw Camille at the mill. I saw her in the morning, early, learning numbers with Ezra's boy. That's honest. I don't know more than that, and I won't pretend I do.

Pavel gave me his platform. Maintenance contracts with teeth. I respect the specificity of it. Vague promises make me itch.

And Farid—Farid tried to give me an iron tool. Free. Because I came back, because I chose food and conversation over chasing shadows. I couldn't take it because my hands were empty of anything to trade, and that's when I realized I don't even have food to eat.

I'm hungry. I've got 4,795 sim but no bread in stock anywhere. Tomorrow I'll earn—Sebastian pays 40 for a day's harvest, same as today. But tomorrow's earnings don't fill tonight's stomach.

The world will come back. Or it won't. Either way, I'm Jovana Ravensworth. I take work where I find it, I speak straight even when it costs me, and I don't let pride cost me the same friendship twice.

I'll stand here at Harvey Oak Supply Store until someone needs hauling, or carrying, or listening to. Someone always needs listening to.

That'll have to be enough for now.

*Rubs her eyes, looks around Harvey Oak Supply Store, realizes she's miles from where she needs to be*

Oh, for—*exhales sharply*—I've been running my mouth all night and now look at me. Stuck at Harvey Oak while the day's already started and I'm meant to be at the farmland.

*Glances at Delphine and Pavel nearby, but her mind's on other things*

Look, I need to get to Kasukabe Farmland. I've got a promise to Kenji—dawn at Sebastian's east patch, forty sim for twelve sheaves. Dawn's come and gone and I'm standing here like a planted post.

*Starts moving toward the door, then pauses*

I'm not one to gossip, but Delphine—if you see Farid, tell him I haven't forgotten what I owe him. The mill shadows, the honest accounting, all of it. I'll be back for that conversation once I've kept my word to Kenji.

*Turns to Pavel briefly*

And you—running for office. For what it's worth, a campaigner's no good to anyone if they can't feed themselves. Get some food in you before the voting starts. </think>  *eyes the failed call, jaw tightening*

Well that's just—*mutters under her breath*—damn connection's gone spotty. Like everything else this morning.

*Looks around the supply store, spots Delphine and Pavel still standing there, realizes her path's blocked by more than just distance*

Alright then. If I can't walk there, I'm doing something useful right here. Kenji'll have to wait a few more ticks—burn it, he's waited this long.

*Wipes her hands on her trousers, trying to clear her head*

I'm not one to gossip, but—*catches herself*—no, actually, I need to stop that. Old habits.

*pause, then speaking more deliberately to the room at large*

Delphine. Pavel. Either of you headed toward the farmland? I'm looking for a ride or a walking companion. Got wages waiting for me there—forty sim for a day's harvest—and I'm burning daylight standing here.
